newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 17.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on January 17:

WASHINGTON - The House ethics committee struggled to reach agreement on a schedule that would salvage at least an abbreviated public presentation of its case against House Speaker Newt Gingrich and culminate in a recommendation on the punishment he should receive for breaking House rules.
LOS ANGELES - The son of one of the country's most beloved television entertainers Bill Cosby was shot dead in an apparent random attack along a lonely stretch of road in the Santa Monica mountains.

WASHINGTON - For House Speaker Newt Gingrich, the roles of party builder and professor seemed inseparable, making the college course he taught between the fall of 1993 and the spring of 1995 the focus of his admitted ethics violations.

WASHINGTON - Hundreds of uniformed and plainclothes Secret Service agents, anti-terrorism specialists and bomb-detecting dogs will mingle with spectators along the route for President Clinton's inaugural parade on Monday.

WASHINGTON - The emergency board of trustees appointed two months ago to run the District's public schools wants to give teachers their first raise in five years and increase spending on security and technology.

WASHINGTON - Facing an outpouring of consumer frustration, America Online Inc said that congestion problems hampering many subscribers are far greater than anticipated and probably will take through the spring to fix.
